provenance.citation: Marr, D., & Poggio, T. (1976). Cooperative computation of stereo disparity. Science, 194(4262), 283–287. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.968816
provenance.locus: Fig. 3 and "Examples of Applying the Algorithm" (p. 285): random-dot stereogram with 50% density, 7 disparity layers (−3 to +3), converging over 14 iterations to reveal an inverted wedding-cake foreground square at disparity +3 against background at disparity 0. Parameters: θ=3.0, ε=2.0, M=5.
provenance.notes: The 1976 Marr-Poggio paper does not contain a multi-object spatial scene with explicit support/above/adjacent relationships in the STRIPS/blocks-world sense. Its concrete worked example is the random-dot stereogram of Fig. 3: a 50%-density stereogram with a central square region at disparity +3 pixels floating above background at disparity 0, solved in 14 iterations. The two governing constraints are R1 (uniqueness — each image element gets at most one disparity, enforced by inhibition along lines of sight) and R2 (continuity — disparity varies smoothly, enforced by excitation along iso-disparity diagonals). The existing fixture in breed-inputs-real.ts uses a blocks-world scene (cube/sphere/pyramid/cylinder with supported_by relationships), which is more characteristic of Marr's 2.5D sketch from his 1982 book. This extraction is adapted from the paper's actual Fig. 3 stereogram example, re-encoding the disparity-layer network state as BreedInput beliefs and goals. The depth relationship (foreground_square nearer than background_field by 3 disparity units) is the direct output the cooperative algorithm produces.

input.intent: resolve stereo disparity correspondence for random-dot stereogram — find stable 2.5D depth grouping via cooperative uniqueness and continuity constraints

expected.algorithm_outcome: cooperative_fixed_point_reached — uniqueness constraint eliminates false targets via lateral inhibition; continuity constraint propagates correct disparity values via excitation along iso-disparity diagonals; network converges to globally stable perceptual grouping with foreground square perceptually segregated from background
